winners.premise: A father presents his daughter with a bill for raising her during her wedding and asks the groom to guarantee repayment.
winners.conflict: A bride must distinguish helping a parent from accepting that her childhood was a debt transferred to her husband.
winners.twist: The father expects the groom's income to make his daughter collectible, revealing that the wedding is what prompted his demand.
winners.hook: Her father demanded thirty thousand dollars for raising her. He presented the bill at her wedding and asked her husband to guarantee it.
winners.narration: Sophie opened the envelope expecting a card. There were figures for food, shoes, school uniforms, and a bank account at the bottom. Her father, Alan, was still holding the microphone. People laughed because they thought it was a joke. He told the groom, James, they could arrange monthly payments. He asked James to guarantee them. James stopped smiling. Sophie asked her father whether he was serious. He said she'd understand what children cost when she had her own. Her mother reached for the microphone, but Sophie asked her to wait. She wanted the answer from him. Alan said James earned enough, and parents deserved something back. Sophie asked whether he'd brought the same bill if she'd married someone earning less. He said that wasn't the point. She asked what the point was, then. Was he in trouble and asking for help, or saying she'd owed him money since she was a child? Alan said he wasn't begging. He'd done his duty, and now it was hers. James put the envelope down instead of putting it in his pocket. Sophie told her father she could discuss help another day. She wouldn't promise payments for having been his daughter. Alan said she was embarrassing him in front of everyone. The microphone was still in his hand. Sophie waited until he looked at it. Then she went back to her husband. Her father kept the envelope.
winners.title: The Invoice in Her Father's Wedding Envelope
winners.description: A father's wedding envelope contains a bill for raising his daughter, with repayment expected from the newlyweds.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT WASNT HER DEBT

winners.premise: A bride uninvites only the groom's daughter from their wedding, keeps her nephews invited, and tells his ex-wife he agreed.
winners.conflict: A father must decide whether to make wedding promises to someone who treats his daughter as a family he should leave behind.
winners.twist: The supposed child-free decision applies only to his daughter, and the bride has used his name to make the exclusion look mutual.
winners.hook: The bride uninvited only the groom's daughter from their wedding. Her nephews were still coming, and she'd told his ex-wife he agreed.
winners.narration: Tom found out when his ex-wife called to ask whether he wanted Mia's flower-girl dress returned. He asked why. Six-year-old Mia had been told the wedding had no place for her. Across the room, Laura was fixing bows on her nephews' jackets. Tom asked why she'd told Mia's mother he'd agreed. Laura said their wedding should mark the beginning of their family. He asked why that required his daughter to disappear from it. Laura told him he was twisting her words. She'd wanted one day without his old life taking over. Tom said Mia wasn't an old life. She was his child. Laura said everybody was waiting and they could discuss visits after the honeymoon. Tom called Mia's mother back. Mia wanted to know whether she'd done something wrong with the petals at rehearsal. He said no. Then she asked whether he was still coming to read her a story that night. He'd promised before any of this happened. Laura held out the ring box and asked whether he was really choosing his ex-wife. Tom told her he was choosing to be honest before making any more promises. The ceremony wasn't going ahead that evening. He put the ring box down. Later, Mia opened the door in pajamas, with her book already chosen. Her pink dress hung behind her. She didn't have to put it on to have her dad beside her.
winners.title: The Flower-Girl Dress She Didn't Need to Wear
winners.description: A groom discovers his daughter alone has been excluded from the wedding, forcing him to confront what his bride means by a new family.
winners.payoff: She didn't have to put it on to have her dad beside her.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF SHE WAS ALREADY FAMILY

winners.premise: A boss announces that an employee will flirt with the landlord for cheaper office rent, then makes coworkers' jobs her supposed responsibility.
winners.conflict: An employee must insist on professional negotiations while her manager turns rent pressure into an expectation of personal availability.
winners.twist: The employee has prepared actual rent figures, while the boss treats her appearance and evening as the business's bargaining tools.
winners.hook: Her boss announced she'd flirt for cheaper office rent. Then he told the staff their jobs depended on her getting a yes.
winners.narration: Priya thought the dinner invitation was for a rent negotiation. She'd spent two days preparing figures. Her boss, Martin, told her to leave those at the office and wear something more interesting than her work jacket. Then he asked the team to wish her luck saving their jobs. Priya said she hadn't agreed to a date. Martin said nobody was asking her to marry the man. She only had to make him feel special. A coworker asked whether she couldn't just be nice for one evening. Priya asked whether his job description included that too. Martin pulled her aside and said refusing would look terrible if somebody had to go. She took her figures to the meeting anyway. The landlord asked why she'd brought a folder to dinner. Martin laughed and said Priya always took work too seriously. She said she'd understood they were discussing the office rent. The landlord said they were; he'd expected Martin to bring a proposal. Priya opened the folder. Their unused storage floor was costing more than the discount Martin wanted. The landlord asked Martin whether he wanted to give it up. Martin hadn't looked at the figures. He asked Priya to stay for drinks while they sorted it out. She said they could arrange a meeting during office hours. She left copies of the figures on the table, put on her work jacket, and went home.
winners.title: The Folder She Was Told to Leave Behind
winners.description: An employee prepares for a rent negotiation, then learns her boss expects flirting rather than a professional proposal.
winners.payoff: put on her work jacket, and went home.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF THAT WASNT HER JOB

winners.premise: A man finds his missing car being auctioned by the police officer who took his report, after his son donated it without permission.
winners.conflict: A father must reclaim a vehicle used for family care while his son treats a charitable intention as permission to give away someone else's property.
winners.twist: The officer believed the son's claim of permission, while the supposedly spare car is what the father uses to take the son's grandmother to appointments.
winners.hook: A man found his missing car being auctioned by a policeman. His son had donated it without asking, then let Dad report it stolen.
winners.narration: Frank recognized the dent above the rear wheel before he saw the charity ribbons. The officer holding the microphone had taken his report four days earlier. Frank called out that it was his car. His son, Daniel, stepped out from behind the auction table and asked him not to make a scene. The officer said Daniel had described it as a family donation. Frank asked his son when he'd agreed. Daniel said he'd wanted to surprise him with something good. He'd sat beside Frank while he called the station about the missing car. Now he said the money would help people, and Dad hardly drove it anyway. Frank opened the boot. His mother's walking frame was still inside. Daniel had never asked why it stayed there. Frank took her to appointments twice a week. Daniel said they could work something out. Frank asked whether he'd meant to volunteer his own car for that, or keep volunteering somebody else's. The officer put down the microphone and stopped taking bids. Daniel looked toward the waiting crowd. Frank told him he could explain the donation himself. So Daniel said the car wasn't his to give. He had to say it loudly enough for the people he'd invited. Frank drove his car home. The next Tuesday, he arrived at Grandma's door in his own car. Frank handed him the walking frame. There wasn't a crowd for that part.
winners.title: The Charity Ribbons on His Missing Car
winners.description: A father's missing car turns up at a charity auction, where his son's generous gesture depends on permission he never had.
winners.payoff: There wasn't a crowd for that part.
winners.like_cta: LIKE IF HELP STARTS WITH ASKING
